title: catch-up 1: the hub's per-room fanout sequence
description:
docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §4. Assign and persist a monotonic per-room sequence, from 1, one per fanout, covering handshakes as well as application messages, never reused or renumbered. It is not a timestamp, not an MLS epoch, not a message id: accepted_timestamp is milliseconds and is not an ordering key (collisions, and no monotonicity across a clock adjustment).

Carry it BESIDE the message in the POST /notify/{roomId} envelope, not inside FanoutMessage (§4 reading 2, the note's recommendation, subject to Mark settling open question 1). That keeps a structure other implementations already parse unchanged, and the sequence is a property of the delivery rather than of the message.

Store it with the hub's fanout so §3's catch-up can serve by sequence. Fixture tests: a sequence is assigned per fanout in hub order; it survives a restart; it does not restart or skip; two fanouts in the same millisecond get distinct increasing sequences.
